subtitle: How Rājaśekhara Measured the World with Poetry

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide inside a lamplit royal library
panels.action: Rājaśekhara stands before towering shelves of palm-leaf manuscripts, one hand on a partially unrolled folio of Kavyamimamsa, Kannauj’s palace city faintly visible through a lattice behind him.

dialogue.text: In Gurjara-Pratihara Kannauj, court poet Rājaśekhara dared to ask: can poetry become a science of the world—and will that science outlive the empire that sponsors it?

i18n.hi: गुर्जर-प्रतिहार काल के कन्नौज में दरबारी कवि राजशेखर ने पूछा: क्या कविता दुनिया का विज्ञान बन सकती है—और क्या यह विज्ञान उसके साम्राज्य से भी ज़्यादा टिकेगा?

panels.shot: slow push-in from balcony down to bustling city and palace complex
panels.action: From a high terrace, Rājaśekhara gazes over Kannauj’s crowded streets, temple spires and palace roofs as traders, scholars and messengers move like small currents below.

dialogue.text: Around 900 CE, Kannauj is a beating heart of power. Under the Gurjara-Pratiharas, it draws merchants, monks and poets from across the Sanskrit world into its stone and dust.

i18n.hi: लगभग ९०० ई में कन्नौज सत्ता की धड़कन है। गुर्जर-प्रतिहारों के अधीन यह व्यापारियों, भिक्षुओं और कवियों को पूरे संस्कृत संसार से पत्थर और धूल के बीच खींच लाता है।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in royal hall with king off-frame, focus on the poet
panels.action: Rājaśekhara stands slightly to the side in a royal audience hall, palm-leaf bundle in hand, as courtiers in rich textiles sit arranged before a shadowed throne.

dialogue.text: Rājaśekhara serves at court, praised for drama and verse. But in his study he begins a different work—a treatise on how poetry itself is made, taught and judged.

i18n.hi: राजशेखर दरबार में नाटक और काव्य के लिए प्रशंसित है। पर अपनी कोठरी में वह नई रचना शुरू करता है—कविता कैसे बनती, सिखाई और परखी जाती है, इस पर एक ग्रंथ।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of hands and manuscript on a low desk
panels.action: By a flickering oil lamp, Rājaśekhara’s hand carefully inscribes characters on a palm leaf labeled Kavyamimamsa, other leaves stacked in ordered piles around him.

dialogue.text: He calls it Kavyamimamsa—an inquiry into poetry. Not just rules, but a map of inspiration, training, beauty, fault, borrowing, and even the lands where poets work.

i18n.hi: वह इसे ‘काव्यमीमांसा’ नाम देता है—कविता पर विचार। सिर्फ नियम नहीं, प्रेरणा, अभ्यास, सौंदर्य, दोष, अनुकरण, और कवियों की भूमियों की पूरी नक़्शा-कथा।

panels.shot: slow push-in to Rājaśekhara seated with young disciples
panels.action: Rājaśekhara sits cross-legged before a small group of students in a quiet cloister, holding a manuscript as the pupils listen intently, slate boards resting at their sides.

dialogue.text: In its surviving chapters, he speaks directly to students of poetry: how to be trained, how to recognize faults and excellences, how to discipline feeling into form.

i18n.hi: बचे हुए अध्यायों में वह सीधे कवि-शिष्यों से बोलता है: कैसे सधे, कैसे गुण-दोष पहचानें, कैसे भाव को अनुशासन में ढालकर रूप दें।

panels.shot: close-up on his face, eyes lifted as if receiving a distant voice
panels.action: Rājaśekhara looks up from his manuscript toward an unseen space, expression thoughtful, as smoke from the lamp curls upward.

dialogue.text: He writes of poetic inspiration as something both mysterious and trainable—an inner wind that must be guided by study, practice and attention to earlier masters.

i18n.hi: वह कवि-प्रेरणा को रहस्यमय पर साधने योग्य बताता है—भीतर की हवा, जिसे अध्ययन, अभ्यास और पुराना साहित्य पढ़कर दिशा देनी होती है।

panels.shot: medium shot with two students reciting while he listens
panels.action: A student recites a verse before Rājaśekhara; the poet leans forward, fingers lightly raised, evaluating as another student watches anxiously.

dialogue.text: He catalogs faults: forced metaphors, clumsy sound, misplaced emotion. And he identifies beauties—suggestion, grace, precision—teaching how to hear quality, not just cleverness.

i18n.hi: वह दोष गिनता है: ज़बरदस्ती के रूपक, भद्दी ध्वनि, बे-मौक़ा भाव। और वह गुण बताता है—संकेत, माधुर्य, सटीकता—सिखाता है कि कौशल कैसे सुना जाए, सिर्फ चालाकी नहीं।

panels.shot: low, thoughtful angle as he pulls out older manuscripts
panels.action: Rājaśekhara opens a chest filled with older palm-leaf manuscripts, placing one beside his work, measuring lines across them with a calm, weighing gaze.

dialogue.text: But he knows no poem is born in emptiness. In one chapter he turns to borrowing—how new poets may take from old works without merely copying them.

i18n.hi: पर वह जानता है, कोई कविता शून्य में नहीं जन्मती। एक अध्याय में वह ‘अनुकरण’ पर आता है—नए कवि पुरानी रचनाओं से कैसे लें, बिना बस नकल किए।

panels.shot: diagrammatic overhead shot of manuscripts radiating out around him
panels.action: Seen from above, Rājaśekhara sits surrounded by open manuscripts, lines and diagrams drawn on a board as if mapping connections among verses.

dialogue.text: He distinguishes kinds of reuse—echo, transformation, close following—and judges them on artistry. Skillful borrowing becomes homage; lazy repetition, a fault.

i18n.hi: वह पुनर्निर्माण की किस्में अलग करता है—प्रतिध्वनि, रूपांतरण, निकट अनुकरण—और उन्हें कला के आधार पर परखता है। कुशल उधार श्रद्धांजलि बनता है; आलसी दुहराव, दोष।

panels.shot: medium shot with him addressing a skeptical student
panels.action: A student questions him, brows drawn; Rājaśekhara answers steadily, hand resting on the manuscript, in a quiet corridor.

dialogue.speaker: rajashekhara
dialogue.text: We live among other poets’ words. The test is not escape, but how we reshape them.

i18n.hi: हम दूसरों की पंक्तियों के बीच जीते हैं। परीक्षा भागने की नहीं, उन्हें नया रूप देने की है।

panels.shot: slow pull-back to reveal wall-hanging map and manuscripts
panels.action: Rājaśekhara stands beside a rough painted map on cloth, rivers and cities marked, while Kavyamimamsa leaves lie arrayed on a table beneath it.

dialogue.text: Then his inquiry shifts. He unrolls a bhuvanakosha—a cosmography. He begins to list regions, rivers, and cities, building a world-picture around Kannauj.

i18n.hi: फिर उसकी मीमांसा बदलती है। वह ‘भुवनकोश’ खोलता है—एक विश्व-नक़्शा। वह प्रदेश, नदियाँ, नगर गिनना शुरू करता है, कन्नौज के इर्द-गिर्द पूरी दुनिया रचता है।

panels.shot: close-up on the map with his finger tracing routes
panels.action: His finger traces across painted river-lines and place-names on the cloth, pausing at a marked Kannauj at the centre, then moving outward.

dialogue.text: This geography is not idle curiosity. It shows where Sanskrit learning lives—linking distant courts and temples into one imagined scholarly world.

i18n.hi: यह भूगोल ऊटपटाँग जिज्ञासा नहीं। यह दिखाता है कि संस्कृत विद्या कहाँ बसती है—दूर के दरबारों और देवालयों को एक कल्पित विद्वत्-संसार में जोड़ता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of court hall with map displayed before nobles
panels.action: In a court assembly, Rājaśekhara stands beside the hung map, gesturing toward it as nobles study the spread of named lands and waters.

dialogue.text: For a king of Kannauj, such a map carries quiet power. To name regions and centres of learning is to imagine an imperial reach over culture, not only over armies.

i18n.hi: कन्नौज के किसी राजा के लिए ऐसा नक़्शा मौन शक्ति है। ज्ञान-केन्द्रों के नाम लेना मतलब संस्कृति पर साम्राज्य सोचना, सिर्फ सेना पर नहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of him shelving his manuscript among others
panels.action: In a calm library, Rājaśekhara carefully places the bundled Kavyamimamsa among other works, labeling the spine-strip before stepping back.

dialogue.text: We do not have the full design of his work; only part of a larger project survives. Yet even in fragments we see a single ambition—to order the craft of culture.

i18n.hi: उसके ग्रंथ की पूरी रचना हमारे पास नहीं; बस बड़ा प्रकल्प आंशिक मिला है। फिर भी टुकड़ों में एक ही चाह दिखती है—संस्कृति की कारीगरी को क्रम में बाँधना।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide: fading from lively court to dim, quiet ruins
panels.action: The court hall where Rājaśekhara once stood fades from bright, crowded splendor to a dim, nearly empty space, pillars worn and dust lying where cushions had been.

dialogue.text: The Gurjara-Pratihara state would weaken and fragment. The stone halls fell silent. Yet the palm leaves bearing Kavyamimamsa traveled beyond Kannauj’s decline.

i18n.hi: गुर्जर-प्रतिहार सत्ता ढलकर टुकड़ों में बँटी। पत्थर के सभागार सूने हो गए। पर काव्यमीमांसा लिखी ताड़पत्री कन्नौज के पतन से आगे निकल गई।

panels.shot: montage-style wide of different later scholars with the same manuscript
panels.action: Across three vignettes, later scholars in distant settings—temple school, monastic library, small court—study or copy the same Kavyamimamsa manuscript.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, critics and poets would still read him. Modern editors and translators study his treatise to understand how the Sanskrit cosmopolitan order saw itself.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद तक आलोचक और कवि उसे पढ़ते रहे। आधुनिक संपादक और अनुवादक उसके ग्रंथ से सीखते हैं कि संस्कृत की विश्व-संस्कृति ने खुद को कैसे देखा।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on manuscript leaf, inked title Kavyamimamsa
panels.action: The camera lingers on a single palm leaf, its incised title Kavyamimamsa sharp, the surrounding script dense and deliberate, a scholar’s hand hovering above it.

dialogue.text: In these pages, poetry is not mere ornament. It becomes a way to think about borrowing, training, geography—a method for studying how creation itself works.

i18n.hi: इन पन्नों में कविता सिर्फ सजावट नहीं। यह उधार, साधना, भूगोल पर सोचने का तरीका है—रचना खुद कैसे चलती है, इसे समझने की विधि।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of Rājaśekhara silhouetted against the city and sky
panels.action: Rājaśekhara stands on the city wall at dusk, Kannauj spreading below, manuscript tucked under his arm as the sky darkens and a few stars appear.

dialogue.text: Rājaśekhara’s empire was built of words, maps and measures. When stone kingdoms crumble, such empires endure wherever people still ask how culture is made, and how it should be judged.

i18n.hi: राजशेखर का साम्राज्य शब्दों, नक़्शों और मापों से बना था। जब पत्थर के राज्य ढहते हैं, ऐसे साम्राज्य वहाँ तक टिकते हैं जहाँ लोग अब भी पूछते हैं: संस्कृति कैसे बनती है, और कैसे परखी जाए।

title_i18n.en: Kavyamimamsa Builds an Empire of Words
